markdown_report:
**Evidence and directions.** Three starting insights guide this early-stage search. First, users report that broadly related items displace specific immediate matches. This motivates selecting context according to recent intent. Second, stale interests persist despite coherent recent activity. Longer history therefore needs selective retention, although these qualitative observations do not establish harmful dependence in the trained model. Third, Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin. Embedding similarity scores near 0.5 indicate little average directional alignment, but cannot exclude dimensional collapse [4].

Three literature insights suggest practical directions. NextItNet preserves sequential structure through residual dilated convolutions [1]. Intermediate states offer overlapping, nested receptive fields, not independent temporal bands. SkipRec provides precedent for user-adaptive block skipping [2], but does not implement positionwise aggregation of intermediate states. Sampled-softmax analysis shows that temperature controls emphasis on difficult negatives [3], supporting a simple objective baseline before explicit mining. Sampled training margins remain optimization diagnostics, not evidence of validation or full-catalog performance [5].

**Framework.** Organize interventions by where uncertainty enters: **context selection → causal receptive-field gating; candidate discrimination → sampled-softmax temperature; sparse item identity → jointly trained title/description features**. These target stale context, weak margins, and insufficient identity respectively. None establishes functional compatibility, duplication, or unmet purchasing needs from interactions alone. Gate concentration likewise does not establish historical influence [6].

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Alignment measures hypothesis relevance, not demonstrated improvement.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Causal receptive-field gate [1,2] | 4/7/8/6/4 | A modest adaptation with reusable context selection; explicitly targets stale interests and broad matches and may improve confusing pairs with little code. | Adaptive depth has precedents; user and margin gains remain uncertain, all blocks still execute, and masking needs care. |
| Temperature-controlled sampled softmax [1,3] | 2/7/5/9/3 | Established, inexpensive objective directly targets weak discrimination and supports useful ablations. | Limited novelty and weaker connection to stale interests; hard negatives can be false negatives, and larger margins need not improve HR@10. |
| Scratch-trained pooled title/description fusion | 4/7/7/6/6 | Shared tokens may improve sparse identity and specific matching within one network. | Familiar combination; noisy text, preprocessing cost, and unverified compatibility limit its value. |

**Selected idea: causal receptive-field gating.** At 0% progress, retain this small architectural intervention, with more conservative originality and potential ratings. Within the supplied NextItNet, collect existing residual-block representations and learn positionwise weights over their receptive fields. Compute gates exclusively from same-position causal states. Channel normalization controls depth-dependent feature scales; aggregation preserves the existing feature dimension and item-scoring interface.

This explicitly targets two reported failures: stale interactions dominating current preferences, and broad relevance outranking specific recent matches. It also targets Electronics’ weak lower-tail separation through potentially more discriminative context. None of these improvements is established. Gates can exploit item frequency, history length, or feature magnitude instead of current intent; near-uniform or saturated gates can also add little value.

**Pseudocode:** `states = causal_blocks(masked_embeddings); z = channel_layernorm(states); logits[l] = dot(w[l], z[l]) + b[l]; weights = softmax(logits, depth); features = sum(weights[l] * z[l]); loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positives, negatives)`. Initialize gate weights and biases to zero for uniform aggregation; retain any baseline final feature transformation consistently across variants.

Preserve left-only convolution padding, channel-only `LayerNorm(D)`, padding masks after convolution/normalization/residual stages, and final-nonpadding readout. Exclude padded targets from loss. For stride-one convolutions, compute receptive span as `1 + sum((kernel_size−1)*dilation)` over actual convolution layers. Do not normalize across time.

Prespecify baseline final-layer readout, uniform normalized aggregation, global learned depth weights, and history-dependent gating; consider a parameter-matched pointwise baseline only if budget permits. Keep the backbone, embeddings, dilation schedule, objective, sampling, and training opportunities fixed. Record exact configurations, parameter counts, checkpoint schedule, stopping rule, GPU allocations, and all failures within 43,200 GPU-seconds. These are separate trials, each deploying one checkpoint per category.

Preserve diagnostic interfaces and measured definitions; unavailable category breakdowns remain unavailable. Supplement margins with embedding norms and centered/uncentered singular spectra and RankMe effective rank on fixed nonpadding item/history samples [4]. Gate entropy describes routing, not causation. If the host exposes paired validation outputs, compare fixed recent suffixes against equal-sized recent-event removals and intervene by replacing gates with their training-history mean. Truncation can induce distribution shift. Report paired category wins/losses and stratified-user bootstrap intervals for macro HR@10 differences; intervals exclude seed variability. Apply Holm correction to prespecified comparisons [7].

Keep seeds 0/42/42, all four routes, `DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']`, trial-local artifacts, and limits of 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Synchronize checkpoint configuration and predictor writer. Select exclusively by unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10; diagnostics cannot replace it. Repeated validation selection can overfit [8], so report all attempted configurations, label gains exploratory, and freeze the final configuration before host-only held-out evaluation.

idea.description: Add channel-normalized, causal positionwise aggregation of existing NextItNet residual-block representations, retaining one jointly trained network and one deployed checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Address two observed user failures: stale interests persisting despite coherent recent activity, and broadly related recommendations displacing specific immediate matches. Adaptive context may also improve Electronics’ 12.27% sampled wrong-rank rate and −0.2595 lower-tail margin. These are hypotheses requiring validation; the method does not establish compatibility, duplication, or unmet purchasing needs.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from the supplied corrected NextItNet and retain its embedding dimension, residual blocks, dilation schedule, objective, optimizer, and sampling for the primary architectural comparison. Collect B×L×D block outputs; apply channel-only LayerNorm(D), then compute one scalar gate logit per block and position using a block-specific D-vector and bias. Initialize gate vectors and biases to zero. Softmax across blocks and sum normalized states, retaining the baseline final feature transformation consistently across variants. All blocks execute; intermediate receptive fields are nested and overlapping. Use left-only convolution padding, a zero padding embedding, and masks after every convolution, normalization, residual stage, and aggregation. Exclude padded targets from loss. Gather the maximum nonpadding index for inference, never count minus one; handle empty histories using the host baseline convention. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView, DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), including measured metrics and metric_definitions. Do not invent unavailable category metadata or review content. Keep score computation identical between training, diagnostics, and embedded predictor. Store architecture configuration, normalization and gating parameters, and the single selected state_dict together; update the predictor writer accordingly. Prespecify final-layer, uniform-normalized, global-weight, and adaptive-gate comparisons; a parameter-matched pointwise control is optional within budget. Each trial uses one independently trained network per category, without fusion or averaging. Record exact hyperparameters inherited from the host, evaluation/checkpoint schedule, stopping policy, parameters, GPU usage, and failed attempts before execution; this proposal alone does not supply those baseline values or establish reproducible results. Keep preprocessing/training/evaluation seeds 0/42/42, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, and the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Select solely by unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10. Supplement existing diagnostics with fixed-sample embedding norms and centered/uncentered RankMe spectra for nonpadding item and final-history representations, explicitly using singular-value rather than squared-singular-value weights. Where host outputs permit, use paired user hit differences and within-category bootstrap intervals; these describe uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates. Gate entropy, suffix interventions, and mean-gate replacement are mechanism checks, not explanations of user behavior. Report every attempted configuration and freeze the final choice before held-out evaluation.
idea.pseudocode:
mask = (sequence != 0).unsqueeze(-1)
x = item_emb(sequence) * mask
states = []
for block in existing_nextitnet_blocks:
    # Preserve left-only convolutions and apply masks within every stage.
    x = block(x, mask) * mask
    states.append(x)
z = stack([depth_norm[l](states[l]) * mask for l in depths], dim=2)
# z: B x L x K x D; LayerNorm acts over D only.
# gate_w and gate_b are initialized to zero.
a = einsum('blkd,kd->blk', z, gate_w) + gate_b
alpha = softmax(a, dim=2)
features = sum(alpha.unsqueeze(-1) * z, dim=2) * mask
features = existing_final_transform(features) * mask
loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative, valid=(positive != 0))
# Inference: gather at max index with sequence != 0.
# Preserve host handling for empty histories.
# Score through existing predict_score; save/load this exact network.
# Compare against prespecified controls using pinned macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Positionwise normalized aggregation is a specific, constraint-compatible adaptation of intermediate NextItNet states; SkipRec’s discrete skip/retain mechanism differs.
originality.negative: Adaptive depth, multiscale aggregation, and feature gating have substantial precedent; a seminal novelty claim is unsupported.

future_potential.positive: Offers an inexpensive mechanism to study context selection while retaining the causal convolutional backbone and existing scoring interface.
future_potential.negative: Nested states may be redundant, gates may learn shortcuts, and all blocks execute; predictive or computational gains are unestablished.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds small normalization and gating layers without new datasets, pretrained models, or a new scoring pipeline.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal masking inside blocks, controlled comparisons, diagnostic adaptation, and exact checkpoint/predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: [1] Establishes residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Supplies the retained backbone and nested receptive-field structure; also discusses sampled softmax.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed positionwise aggregation on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: SkipRec: User-Adaptive Layer Selection for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: [2] Provides precedent for user-adaptive block retention or skipping.
limitations: Its skip/retain action selection differs from softmax aggregation of intermediate states.
Does not establish that the proposed gate resolves the supplied user failures.

related_work.title: Wu et al. (2024): Sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: [3] Explains emphasis on high-scoring negatives through sampled-softmax gradients and temperature.
limitations: Does not establish gains on this benchmark.
Stronger emphasis on difficult candidates can amplify false-negative effects.

related_work.title: RankMe
contributions: [4] Supplies an effective-rank diagnostic computed from normalized singular values.
Motivates examining representation dimensionality beyond mean pairwise cosine.
limitations: Effective rank does not establish predictive quality or identify a recommendation failure by itself.
Centered and uncentered spectra and singular-value versus covariance weighting give different measurements.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems
contributions: [5] Supports caution when interpreting evaluation with sampled candidate sets.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator or inferring full-catalog gains from sampled HR@10.

related_work.title: Attention is not Explanation
contributions: [6] Motivates separating learned weighting patterns from evidence of causal influence.
limitations: Studies attention rather than this NextItNet gate; its relevance is methodological.
Gate interventions establish model sensitivity, not causal explanations of user preferences.

related_work.title: Recommender evaluation guidance
contributions: [7] Supports careful experimental design and paired evaluation of recommender differences.
limitations: User-level intervals conditional on fixed models and candidates exclude training-seed and dataset-sampling uncertainty.
Multiplicity adjustment does not eliminate adaptive validation selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: [8] Explains how repeated optimization of a finite validation criterion can overfit model selection.
limitations: Prespecification and complete reporting reduce opportunities for selection bias but do not replace untouched held-out evaluation.
